quests.title: The Tsaritsa's Chess Game (I)

dialogue.t: Trying to put me in check? Careful. If you move forward, my ambush awaits.
We can't go forward or backward. And the white pieces are all protecting each other.
You see, although the black king is still out of reach, I have "checkmated" his queen. What say you of the state of this game now?
Hm, it still doesn't look great for white. Black has a lot of pieces that haven't moved yet.
And thus my solution to this endgame has reached a stalemate...

dialogue.sit: I still think white has a chance to win.

dialogue.t: Oh?

dialogue.sit: You've been focusing on how this game is going to end, but I've been thinking about how it got to this point.
If the white king hadn't offered himself as bait to lure away the black bishop, the black queen wouldn't have successfully been boxed in.
White's remaining pieces might not be as powerful as the queen, but each move is made with intention and meaning.
The black queen naively assumed the white pieces were simply on the retreat, and that's how she fell into their trap.
So, I think white still has a chance to win.

dialogue.t: ...Your analysis has little to do with rules or logic.

dialogue.sit: Rules and logic aren't the only things that determine the outcome of a game. Willpower, determination... Those are important factors too.

dialogue.t: Hm, a pearl of wisdom gleaned from your many brushes with danger and adversity, no doubt. I suppose you have cause to reach such a conclusion. I believe I do have a better understanding of you now, {NICKNAME}.
Chayka.
Yes, Your Majesty.
Elevate {NICKNAME} to the position of "Privy Councilor" and increase {M#his}{F#her} authority by another level. I will have more important tasks to assign to {M#him}{F#her} in the future.
Yes, Your Majesty.
The Consultant has arrived, Your Majesty. I shall take my leave.

dialogue.sit: What can we help you with this time, Your Majesty?

dialogue.t: I would like to know more about... you.
{NICKNAME}?
Not only have you journeyed far across the land, but you hail from beyond this world.
To me, your thoughts and feelings about Teyvat are very valuable indeed. We have agreed to work together, but I've realized there is little I know about you.
Pierro often says a game of chess is the best way to reveal a person's true colors. Do you play too, {NICKNAME}?
Then, perhaps we could walk through a certain endgame scenario together.
No matter. I don't intend to play a full game. I merely wish to walk through a certain endgame scenario together.
I'll offer explanations as we go.
Wow, what a beautiful chessboard! It looks like a collector's item. These pieces actually seem kinda familiar...
It is a collector's item, in a way. Pierro and I never use this board when we play. It's far too ornate. A board and its pieces should be simple.
So it's just part of your collection then?
I have no collection, actually. It was a gift from an old friend. Are you familiar with the name Ioanna Ivanovna?
Don't think so... Is she a friend of yours?
She was the original Mage J.
We often played chess together when she was still alive.
Later, she had this chess set crafted as a gift for me. She said the design of the pieces came from suggestions from some good friends.
She hoped this chess set would be nothing more than a collectible one day, because that would mean I had finally stepped away from the endless machinations and strategizing that consumes my days.
Then, I could put it on display as nothing more than a beautiful thing to adorn these halls.

dialogue.sit: Sounds like she wanted the best for you.

dialogue.t: However, it has been centuries, and still... the chessboard remains.
Even in my spare time, I use it to study various endgame scenarios. Let us begin.
Look at the state of the game. How does each side fare?
Uh... Kinda looks like white is at a disadvantage... They have fewer pieces.
Well-observed. White has sacrificed more than black, that is for certain. They even lost their queen, a most powerful piece indeed.
The black king has not moved at all. He remains seated on his throne. Is it indifference or arrogance behind his inaction? Who can say...
The black queen has already charged into our formation. Just one more step forward, and she'll join forces with the black bishop to put us in check.
So white is about to lose?
You are not so quick to jump to the same conclusion, I imagine?

dialogue.sit: They still have a chance, right?

dialogue.t: ...An astute observation.
Ohhh, so we need to stop the black queen! But that piece is super strong, isn't it? Can we really do it?
The queen is the most powerful piece in chess. In a single move, she can capture any enemy piece that tries to surround her.
But, what if we simply let her? You're playing black now, {NICKNAME}. Have the queen make her move.

quests.description: The Tsaritsa invites you to a battle of wits as a way to better understand how you approach problems. However, one could also see this not just as a battle, but a long heart-to-heart talk...
